subject: Renewal pricing and ramp plan for Q3 expansion
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@urbanstitch.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@urbanstitch.com
Date: 2027-04-17T08:50:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal request + FY28 capacity plan

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the conversations last month. UrbanStitch is planning a Q3 expansion for FY28: we expect a ~2x increase in inference minutes (mainly embedding + chat) over our current commit. Our procurement team asked me to get a firmed renewal quote before we finalize the PO timeline (we'd like pricing to hold for the 12-month renewal term).

High level asks:
- Can Redwood hold existing unit pricing for up to 6 months after the renewal effective date while we ramp usage?
- If we increase committed capacity by 50% today, can we get a bridging credit for the first quarter to offset spike consumption?
- Any discounts available for multi-year or a staged true-up approach?

I attached a short summary (UrbanStitch_Renewal_Request.pdf) with projected ramp. Procurement is on copy — they prefer a commercial answer + an editable amendment that the legal team can quick-review.

Proposed cadence: answer this week so we can include the numbers in our board materials. Can you propose a short commercial sketch and a call tomorrow afternoon?

Thanks,
Elena

Elena Torres
Head of Infrastructure
UrbanStitch

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@urbanstitch.com>
Cc: procurement@urbanstitch.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-17T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal request + FY28 capacity plan

Elena — great to hear and congrats on the growth plan. High level commercial sketch below, happy to refine on a quick call.

1) Term & price hold
- We can offer a 12-month term with a 90-day price hold on current unit rates. If you sign for a 12-month renewal today, the base unit price will be locked for the first 90 days; after that we provide a staged cap with a maximum 6% mid-term adjustment (only if HW/market changes materially).

2) Committed uplift + bridging credit
- Option A (50% commit uplift): 12% one-time bridging credit applied to Q1 invoices (calculated vs incremental usage over current baseline).
- Option B (phased uplift): commit 25% now, additional 25% in month 4 — receive 7% bridging credit for first quarter and a 6% discount on committed units for months 4–12.

3) Multi-year / staged true-up
- 24-month term: additional 4% volume discount on committed units (applies after year 1), limited to baseline + 2x current usage. True-up at each 6-month milestone.

4) Operational asks
- We can stagger invoice timing to match your PO schedule; finance can do 30/60/90 net for committed invoices on request.

Attached: Draft_Term_Amendment_v1.pdf (editable). If this looks directionally helpful I can join procurement call tomorrow.

Would you be available 4/17 3:00pm PT or 4/18 10:00am PT?

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Commercials — Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-17T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal request + FY28 capacity plan — internal pricing posture

Ben / Lauren — forwarding Elena's ask. Quick internal notes and recommendation before I go to the call this afternoon: 

- Customer wants price hold + bridging credit. UrbanStitch is strategic (integration partner with marketplace pipeline) — high expansion potential.
- Recommended commercial posture: offer Option B (phased uplift) as the public offer. Rationale: lowers immediate capacity risk, still gives them credit & an attractive committed discount, keeps runway to convert to 24-month if they accelerate.
- Limits to ask legal/finance for: cap bridging credit at $125k lifetime and ensure credit applies to usage over their baseline only. Finance to confirm we can invoice committed portion on a 60-day net to align with their PO.

Action items: 
- Ben: confirm whether 7% bridging credit + 6% committed unit discount is within quota authority or needs approval.
- Lauren: approve the $125k cap on the credit (or propose alternate cap).

I'll join the call with Elena at 3pm; if you can ping back quickly I can close on the draft and share the DocuSign link.

Thanks — Steph

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@urbanstitch.com>
Cc: procurement@urbanstitch.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal request + FY28 capacity plan — updated offer

Elena — thanks for the call today. Per discussion, here's a concise commercial offer you can share with legal/procurement: 

Summary offer (finalized for PO):
- Term: 12 months starting on effective date in PO.
- Price hold: Current unit price locked for first 90 days post-effective date. After 90 days a capped mid-term adjustment up to 6% applies only if major hardware/market changes occur.
- Commit uplift: 50% immediate committed uplift (applies to embedding + chat clusters).
- Bridging credit: 7% credit on incremental usage above baseline for the first 90 days. Credit limited to $125,000 total; applied as account credit on invoice.
- Phased true-up: if usage exceeds 1.75x baseline by month 6 we automatically reprice the incremental tier at a negotiated volume discount and open a path to a 24-month conversion at +4% off committed units.
- Billing: committed portion invoiced monthly; committed invoice net-60 (to align with your PO). Consumption overages billed monthly at posted rates, with credit applied.

Attached: Updated_Pricing_Sheet.xlsx (detailed math) and I just created a DocuSign envelope for your legal team: https://docusign.com/embedded/abc123-urb-renewal. Please confirm who will sign and the PO number so we can lock the price hold window.

If procurement wants a small amendment, I attached Draft_Term_Amendment_v1.pdf with tracked changes. Happy to loop legal if they want edits.

Thanks — looking forward to finalizing this week.

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Commercials — Redwood Inference
Attachments: Updated_Pricing_Sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet), Draft_Term_Amendment_v1.pdf (editable)
